decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer mentions MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY as a condition but never says it is commented out in the shipped mbedtls_config.h; it even says the config default is unverified.

decisions.mark: concludes that in a DEFAULT build there is no indirection at all — mbedtls_calloc and mbedtls_free are preprocessor macros expanding directly to calloc and free
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer says the default build uses function pointers in platform.c, and only the MEMORY-undefined case maps to calloc directly. It never concludes that the default build has no indirection with macros expanding to calloc/free.

decisions.mark: distinguishes the two ways to substitute an allocator — a COMPILE-time pair of macros versus a RUNTIME pair of function pointers — and states that they are mutually exclusive
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Runtime, the common route. Enable `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_C` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` but not the two macros. ... Compile time. Define `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO` | WHY: The answer separates the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer pair. It says the runtime route requires "but not the two macros", and its diagram shows the pointer path only when no macros are set. That states they are mutually exclusive.

decisions.mark: states that on the macro path mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free does not exist at all — it is neither declared nor compiled, rather than being present and ignored
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer never says that on the macro path mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free is neither declared nor compiled. It says only that call sites expand directly to the user's function.

decisions.mark: identifies that the pointers' defaults FAIL rather than fall back — an uninitialised calloc returns NULL and an uninitialised free does nothing
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer says that with `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_NO_STD_FUNCTIONS` the calloc default becomes `platform_calloc_uninit`, which always returns NULL. It never says that the free default does nothing. It also doesn't frame these defaults as failing rather than falling back.

decisions.mark: identifies the buffer allocator (MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C) as the only in-tree user of the runtime setter, installing itself over the pointers from its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The library's only use of this facility is its own stack-based allocator, `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init`. ... `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init` (memory_buffer_alloc.c:566) is the library's own use of the hook. ... installs its own functions through `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free`. | WHY: The answer names the buffer allocator's init function as the library's only user of the setter, which installs its own functions over the pointers. It doesn't spell out the macro MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C, but the module and mechanism are clearly identified.

decisions.mark: states that the buffer allocator installs a MUTEXED pair when MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is on and a plain pair otherwise, chosen at compile time inside its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: It zeroes its heap, creates a mutex when `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is set, and installs its own functions through `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free`. It uses the mutexed variants when threading is on, and the plain ones otherwise. | WHY: The answer states that the init function installs mutexed allocator variants when threading is on and plain ones otherwise, and ties this to `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`. It doesn't use the words "compile time", but the macro gate makes that implicit.

decisions.mark: states that the buffer allocator itself requires MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY, so enabling it alone is not enough to route the library's allocations through it
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator calls mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free but never states that the allocator itself requires MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY, so enabling that option alone is not enough.
